headline.title: Pre-season: cold nights ahead.
headline.text: 17 of the 25 resorts close to opening get nights cold enough to make snow, mostly in White Mountains and Northern Vermont. Killington typically opens first, around Nov 8.

BTV.excerpt:
Large ridge of surface high pressure will keep conditions dry with seasonable temperatures through late week.
Dry and seasonable conditions continue through the beginning of next week.

ALY.excerpt: ) Dry conditions are expected to continue through next Monday.

GYX.excerpt: High pressure remains in control of the weather pattern across northern New England through the weekend while an ocean storm passes offshore.

BUF.excerpt: ) Dry and tranquil weather will prevail through the weekend.

PHI.excerpt:
A well offshore nor'easter bringing coastal impacts and hazardous marine conditions through Thursday.
A prolonged period of onshore flow will lead to multiple elevated high tide cycles this week resulting in rounds of coastal flooding.
Frost impacts possible Friday night and Saturday night where the growing season continues.

CTP.excerpt: ) Dry and seasonable weather continues into the last week of October

RLX.excerpt: ) High pressure ruling the roost through the weekend will continue to provide extended dry weather, with near seasonable daytime temperatures, while chilly overnights with patchy frost potential and river valley steam fog.

writeups.name: Vermont
writeups.title: Dry, with cold nights.
paras: Next two days: summit temperatures from {{t:25}} to {{t:49}}, mostly dry.
Killington usually opens first here, around Nov 8. Jay Peak gets the most hours cold enough to make snow this week (about 36).
NWS Burlington forecasters, Tuesday 7:20 PM: "Large ridge of surface high pressure will keep conditions dry with seasonable temperatures through late week."
writeups.outlook: Days 8 to 14: NOAA's outlook leans slightly warmer than normal and near-normal precipitation.
